To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular classification of diffuse gliomas, based on the presence of IDH mutation and 1p/ 19q codeletion in astrocytomas and oligodendroglicomas, is refined by adding ATRX loss of expression, resulting in 4 molecularly distinct groups of gliomas that are associated with different prognosis.
the ATRX gene is mutated and/or deleted in 30% of gliomas, and loss of ATRx expression defines a group of gliomas with a better prognosis.
the loss of ATRXR expression defines 4 prognostically distinct groups of gliomas irrespective of diagnosis and grade.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel molecular classification of glioma, which is based on IDH mutation status, 1p19q codeletion and ATRX protein loss.
the identification of new markers that may be used to better characterize glioma subgroups, to improve their prognostic stratification, and to guide the choice of the most appropriate treatment.
the development of a new classification system for gliomas that integrates molecular markers and clinical features.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATRX protein loss is a common feature of diffuse astrocytic gliomas, but is rare in glioblastomas, oligodentrogliomas, or glioblastoma with oligodendroglic component.

molecular classification of glioma based on IDH mutation, ATRX expression and 1p/9q codeletion is more informative and useful than histopathology and WHO grade for predicting the outcome of the patients.

ATRX expression is a marker of good prognosis in diffuse astrocytic tumors with an astroglial component and that it is a marker that can refine the molecular classification of diffuse astrocytic gliomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ATRX expression is a new marker for molecular classification of glioma, which can be used to distinguish prognostically different subgroups of patients.
the ATRX protein is a novel molecular marker for the classification of diffuse gliomas and that it is a strong independent predictor of overall survival in patients with astrocytomas.

the loss of expression of ATRX protein, in combination with IDH mutation and 1p/1q codeletion, defines 4 molecular groups of gliomas (IDH-mutant/ATRX-proficient, IDH-mutant and ATRX-deficient, IDH-wild-type and 1p19q codeleted, and IDH-wild type and ATRX-proficient) with distinct clinical and molecular characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular classification of diffuse gliomas is more accurate than their histological classification, and it is independent of diagnosis and grade.
molecular markers can be used to define new prognostic groups, which are independent of histology or grade.
the molecular classification of diffuse gliomas should take into account ATRX expression.
